name: Audio base latency
plain: AudioContext.baseLatency reveals the audio stack and hardware.
meaning: Typical values 0.005 to 0.04 seconds depending on OS and driver (macOS about 0.01, Windows 0.01 to 0.03, Android up to 0.04). Mild hardware signal; read without playing sound.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can measure your audio delay to guess your system and audio hardware
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Check the audio delay, usually 0.005 to 0.04 seconds
Guess your system, such as macOS, Windows or Android
Do this without playing any sound
cannot: Listen to you or record sound
Name your exact headphones or speakers
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A page reads how long your audio system takes to start sound, which hints at your hardware.

marketing.name: AudioContext.baseLatency
marketing.pitch: Reports the delay the audio system adds, so apps can keep sound and visuals in sync.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. You just get better timed sound in games and music apps. The same number can quietly tell a site if you use a phone, a laptop or a studio sound card.
story.for_makers: Real time audio apps need this number to line sound up with the screen. Trackers and fraud tools add it to a device profile since it differs by hardware and operating system.

use_cases.example: A browser rhythm game uses your audio delay to shift the note timing so the beat matches what you hear.
A web music maker adjusts its recording delay so a track recorded from the mic lines up with the backing.
A video call tool tunes its audio buffer to avoid echo and lag on your headset.
A live streaming page keeps the sound and the picture aligned by checking audio output delay.
A fraud tool sees an audio delay typical of a virtual machine and raises the risk.
A tracker puts the delay value in a device ID along with other audio numbers.
A web music lesson app checks delay so it can tell you whether you played in time.

history.change: Web audio readback restricted for known fingerprinters
